title: Tool pack meta.json
description: skills/faion/tools/<pack>/meta.json. One meta.json per pack directory gates its scripts and its cards. A pack without meta.json inherits the skill-level tier silently, which is why the file is required rather than optional. Enforced by scripts/validate-tools.py.

slug.description: Pack identity in the tier manifest. Suffixed -tools so a pack slug can never collide with a tool name.

tier.description: Gate for every script and card in the pack. A fragment that names a tool must be gated at or above the tool's tier, or the instruction is uninvokable for the user who can read it.

summary.description: What the pack holds, named tool by tool. Copied verbatim into tools/INDEX.xml, where it is the only thing an agent reads before deciding whether a tool already exists for its job.

network.description: Present only when a tool in the pack opens a socket. Absent means the pack is offline, and validate-tools.py fails any script that imports a network module without it.

hosts.description: Every host the pack's scripts may contact. A URL literal naming a host that is not listed is a finding — the allowlist is what stops a credential leaving for somewhere it was never scoped to.

class.description: read: the pack issues no non-GET request. mutate: it can write, so every writing tool is dry-run until --yes, prints the change set first, and caps it. There is deliberately no 'destroy' class — an irreversible delete does not ship, so DELETE cannot be committed.

credentials.description: Present only when a tool needs a third-party secret. The secret is read from the environment and nowhere else: never a flag (argv lands in shell history and in ps), never a file the tool reads by convention, never cached — note that ~/.faion/tools/<pack>/ is world-readable.

env_var.description: The single environment variable holding the token.

min_scope.description: The least privilege that makes the pack work, named in the vendor's own permission vocabulary, so a user can create a token that cannot do more than the pack needs.
